quests.name: Valley of Bones
quests.objective: Improve your reputation with the Gelkis, and locate Nerlokh near the Valley of Bones far east of Gelkis Village.
quests.description:
One of our scouts returned to the village while you were away, with news that confirmed my fears.

The Magram are up to something, <name>. It is not good.

The Valley of Bones far to the east is a cursed land that few centaur dared to enter and fewer still ever return home. Our enemy has found something there, something evil, and we need to learn what it is.

Seek out the scout Nerlokh at the southern entrance, but you may have to prove yourself further to the Gelkis.
quests.progress: You must be the ally that Uthek spoke of. I am Nerlokh of the Gelkis, but our time for introductions stops there.
quests.completion:
Behold, the Valley of Bones. Forever cursed, a place where not even the great Theradras would smile upon. No clan had dared to step hoof in this place for generations, yet now the Magram seem to have claimed it as their own!

I am poorly trained and unequipped for combat--these arches are the farthest I will go. You, <name>, must fight on behalf of the Gelkis.

You have done much for us, but your work has only begun.

quests.name: Ravaging Ravagers
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan and slay 6 Undead Ravagers, then return to Nerlokh at the southern entrance to Valley of Bones.
quests.description:
You need not peer far to see the undead shambling about ahead of us, but have you noticed something unusual about them?

They walk on two legs, not four! These skeletons are not even our fallen kin. The Magram must be defiling the bodies of those who died long before the Desolace was our domain. I cannot imagine how they justified turning their backs on Mother Theradras and took to desecrating corpses that have rested here for centuries.

Put the undead to rest, <name>.
quests.progress: Be swift and merciful, <name>. Whoever these bones belong to were never meant to be a part of our war.
quests.completion:
You looked battered and beaten, but not broken. Your efforts have made a difference to those that have been put back to rest, but I am sure you have noticed the turmoil in the valley has only risen.

I fear it won't be long before those same bones you buried are back on their feet.

We must press on.

quests.name: Facing the Truth
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan, and bring an Accursed Skull and Gelkis Necromantic Garb to Uthek the Wise in Gelkis Village.
quests.description:
This discovery is devastating for our clan, but it is in our best interest to keep this only to those who need to know. Uthek is one such person who needs to be aware of what is going on here. I suspect she will know how to proceed.

Take this to show her. For good measure, we should also bring evidence of the necromancy itself to her. Find a skull that looks recently cursed. I suspect they may be hoarding them in the maws of one of the goliath's skeletons.
quests.progress: I did not expect to see you back so soon. Is this a bad omen?
quests.completion:
<Uthek listened to your explanation with an expression of doubt, until you presented the material evidence.>

I noticed our dwindling numbers, <name>, but never would I have expected this! Necromancy... shamelessly wielded by those foul Magram. Now I learn that my clan is involved too?

I will speak with the Khan. For now, you will prepare to return to the front lines.

quests.name: Valley of Bones
quests.objective: Improve your reputation with the Magram, and locate Orgrul near the Valley of Bones south of Magram Village.
quests.description:
It is time, outsider, for you to learn of our great discovery... but Warug will not be the one to tell it!

Head south to the other end of the village. Look for a big, stinky centaur named Orgrul.

You will know when you get there.
You will know when you see him.
If he thinks you deserve to know, you will know.

And if he doesn't? Well. You can be happy knowing Warug has a new crown.
quests.completion:
So the rumors are true. Unfortunate that Warug has had you running around with frivolous tasks. At least you proved your worth.

Peer down into the valley below, what do you see? Bones and bodies. Roaming undead. And the Twin Goliaths.

This place was cursed long before our arrival, and I suspect it will remain as such for many generations to come. Our clan was the first to brave the horrors below, and ours will be the only one to claim its power.

Are you as eager as I to rule over all of Desolace?

quests.name: Outcast Necromancers
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and slay Outcast Necromancers within the Valley of Bones.
quests.description:
Have you noticed the puny centaur stomping about around here? Those are of Gelkis descent.

We Magram have already established a foothold deeper into the canyon. When the Gelkis took notice of our presence here, some among them chose to follow in our footsteps. I know not whether they wish to join us or attempt to overthrow us, but I do know that their clanmates have sentenced them all to exile.

They're lone wolves meddling in powers that do not belong to them. I want them dead.
quests.progress: Take note of the color of their flesh and fur, <race>. We will know if you kill any of ours, and such an act will not reflect kindly upon you.
quests.completion:
Bwahaha, I heard their cries from here!

The Gelkis ought to learn to slaughter their own kin who betray their heritage. Failing to do so puts the burden on us to clean up their mess, and I am not here to tidy up after an inferior clan.

If you see more, be sure to snuff out the lights in their eyes. Once a Gelkis, always a Gelkis.

quests.name: Bone Raising
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram Clan, and use the Enhanced Necromancy Staff to fully raise undead that are struggling to emerge throughout the Valley of Bones. Return to Orgrul once the Magram army has grown.
quests.description:
I can see the excitement in your eyes, outsider. Do you grasp the potential of necromancy yet?

Of course you do. And that is why I am ordering you to hone your skills further.

As you venture deeper into the Valley of Bones, you will see the remains of failed attempts at raising the dead. Gelkis attempts, no doubt. Hardly able to claw out from the dirt. Funny, were it not so pathetic.

I have imbued your staff with greater power. Use this to grow our army, and crush the ones that fight back!
quests.progress: Look for bones partially emerged from the soil in the Valley of Bones, <race>, and use your staff on them. You will know if it worked, and continue to try even if it doesn't.
quests.completion:
<Orgrul listens to your explanation, unable to suppress a grin.>

Do not fret, outsider, for this experiment was anything but a failure. We now know how weak and fragile the Gelkis' form of necromancy is. They have a long way to go before they will match our might.

The fact that you were able to seize control of any of them speaks highly of you, too. Despite those wasted skeletons, you have demonstrated your impressive capabilities.

I will take the staff for now. There is more work to do.

quests.name: Outing Outcasts
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan, and bring 1 Necromantic Garb to Nerlokh at the entrance of the Valley of Bones.
quests.description:
While I waited for your arrival, I peered a bit further between the arches and noticed something I need you to confirm for me.

I cannot bear saying it aloud. Not until my suspicions have been proven true.

<name>, while you are getting your bearings in the valley, slay some of the necromancers that look weaker than the others. Tear off their ritual garb, carefully, and bring it to me. I must know whether I am of clear mind and vision.
quests.progress:
You have my word that I will share my suspicion with you once you have completed the task.

For the sake of our clan, let us hope my eyes were playing tricks on me.
quests.completion:
<Nerlokh swiftly takes the cloth and accessories from you and his expression grows cold. After observing only a few from the collection, he sets the rest aside.>

<name>. These lesser necromancers are Gelkis.

I see now why our clan seems to be losing numbers more frequently than our skirmishes would indicate. Some among us are defecting, presumably in effort to impress the Magram.

Our clan is losing this war.

quests.name: Proof of Concept
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram Clan, then bring 426 Well Cursed Bones from a successful ritual back to Orgrul.
quests.description:
We already know these crystals are capable of more than sundering the ground--the Gelkis have proven that they can be twisted for necromantic power. Do you remember the bones I had you collect? I assembled them as best I could just up the hill. There was enough for two workable skeletons.

<Orgrul hands you a newly made staff.>

I will deliver the Necrokhan's staff while you play with your new toy. Return only once you can prove that you know how to use it.
quests.progress: Despite your aid thus far, if you are unable to raise the dead then your usefulness with the Magram has come to an end.
quests.completion:
I can see a new fire burn brightly in your eyes, outsider. You have demonstrated your ability to create your own armaments, summon minions to do your bidding, and most importantly to assert your dominance when they refuse to follow your command.

A shame you have no centaur blood in you. You would be well on your way to become the next Khan.

quests.name: Fragments of the Pylons
quests.objective: Recover shards and fragments of the pylons, found guarded at the Magram and Gelkis villages. Return them to Mordent Evenshade.
quests.description:
Although I am sure we can attribute the damage to both pylons to the reckless centaur stomping about, I suspect the timing of their rampage resulted in the shards being separated. I know little about their quarrels, but I do know there are at least two main factions that have trespassed into Shen'dralas: the ferocious Magram and the cunning Gelkis.

Keeping these treasures in the midst of a battlefield would be unwise. By now, I am assuming they have taken their trophies back to their own villages.
quests.progress: I would rather not further draw the centaur's attention toward me or my fallen kin, else I would seek out the crystals myself.
quests.completion:
The crystals are in a few more pieces than I was expecting, but this looks to be all of it. I will hold onto these for the moment. Thank you, <name>.

Your next step will be to gather mana that is malleable enough to serve as both an adhesive for the broken pieces, and a conduit for the leylines to surge through thereafter.

It is quite a remarkable process, but gathering the mana may prove to be an inconvenience.

quests.name: Mountain of Bones
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and bring 426 Gently Cursed Bones to Orgrul south of the Magram Village in Desolace.
quests.description:
Some sort of necromantic energy has permeated throughout the Valley of Bones, for reasons we have yet to understand.

Those reasons are also of no importance to us. The magic is ours now, and those who do not fight with blade or mallet are trained in this new magic.

If you think I intend to start you off with a challenging task, think again. For now, go into the Valley of Bones and fetch some bones for me. I am sure you can handle that.
quests.progress: For every bone short you are for the task, I will take one of yours to make up the difference.
quests.completion:
<Orgrul begins to count the bones, but begins to skip numbers as they gain a second digit and eventually loses count. He tries a second time, but glares your direction partway through when your expression contorts while observing.>

Bah. I will count them later. This looks like enough. You had best not be deceiving me.

I will hold onto these.

quests.name: Corrupting Tears
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and bring 3 Petrified Bark and 3 Imbued Tears back to Orgrul.
quests.description:
Outsider, did you notice the weapon that the outcast necromancers held in their hands? We will ensure the Gelkis will not live long enough to master the ways of necromancy, but their methods of channeling caught my interest. They even use those same crystals Warug asked you to steal.

I think we can use this technique to our advantage. Venture back into the valley to recover some wood from the accursed trees, and see if Warug will part with some of his crystals. I will make staves from them.
quests.progress: These staves may be the missing piece we need to secure the rest of the Valley of Bones. Go now, <race>, let us make use of the Gelkis' ways before their next discovery.
quests.completion:
Only three? Hmmph, Warug is being stingy as always. Give me a moment while I create the staves.

I will take one. The second will go to the Necrokhan that patrols along the chokepoint toward the elven ruins.

The third is yours. You are a part of this war, now more than ever.

quests.name: No Mercy for the Weak
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram Clan, and slay 5 Gelkis Captives scattered around the Valley of Bones. Return to Orgrul after the task is complete.
quests.description:
As you tread further into the Valley of Bones, you will find Gelkis wanderers that dared to enter our territory. I instructed they be kept alive so they could feed the bone worms burrowing about, but they seem uninterested in their prey being alive.

This task is simple. Find the prisoners, then snuff out their life. Don't give them a brief glimmer of hope for freedom.
quests.completion:
As much as I would have loved to hang their skulls from my tent, their bodies are far more valuable to the Magram left in the valley.

The bone worms will devour their flesh by the next morning, and we will have many new skeletons to raise thereafter.

With each Gelkis death, the Magram army grows stronger!

quests.name: Saving Our Own
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis clan, and rescue 5 Gelkis Captives within the Valley of Bones. Return to Nerlokh near the entrance when you are done.
quests.description:
There was a brief battle between a few of the necromancers just around the hill, and I used that to take a closer look inside.

<name>, not all of our recent losses were defectors. There are Gelkis being held captive further in the valley! I was not able to investigate their situation because a hulking Magram brute started charging my direction. I consider myself fortunate he lost interest quickly.

You must go back into the Valley of Bones and free them. The Gelkis stand together.
quests.completion:
When I first heard the stamping of hooves, I thought I was about to be pushed back to the village. Imagine my delight the moment I saw my brethren retreating past these arches, alive and well!

I have directed the survivors to report to Uthek to share anything they might have learned. I do not anticipate reinforcements, <name>, but this bodes well for the future of our clan.

Let us remain focused in our task.

quests.name: Bone Burying
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan, and dispel the curses from 8 failed summons throughout the Valley of Bones.
quests.description:
About this staff of yours. I recognize it as one of Uthek's, and you mentioned it was constructed with Theradras' Tears, augmented with a Draenethyst Crystal, and that it can dispel dark magic?

I noticed that there are skeletons stuck just underneath the rocky soil further into the valley. I believe these are failed summons from the Outcast Necromancers, doomed perhaps forever to an existence smothered in dirt.

Laying them to rest again would be good for our cause, and their spirits.
quests.completion:
There is a weight lifted off my shoulders knowing that you restored peace to so many bodies.

All my life I expected our clan wars to inevitably end in brutality and bloodshed. Never would I have guessed that I would be staring death in the face, with death staring right back.

Thank you, again, <name>.

quests.name: Phantasmal Problems
quests.objective: Take Vindael's unfinished sword and figure out a way to usher it into the spirit realm, then return the Phantasmal Blade to him at Shen'dralas.
quests.description:
Being corporeal has its challenges, as you know, but being INcorporeal is a whole other situation. Will I fall through THIS chair? Will I trip over THAT cat? Worst of all, however, it makes everyday work impossible!

Do you see this sword on my anvil? I began work on this thousands of years ago, but met my demise before it was finished. Now it taunts me, AND takes up precious real estate! I cannot work with it! I cannot MOVE it!

I need you to help, uh, "ferry" it to the spirit realm. What do you say?
quests.progress: I know of only one way to get things into the spirit realm, <race>, but I am sure you can come up with something better.
quests.completion:
Wait... you did it? Err, I mean... you did it!

My problem was very real but my desired solution certainly was not. I am unsure what surprises me the most. That you made the plunge? That the blade followed you into the spirit realm?

<Vindael eyes you up and down once, then again with suspicion overtaking his expression.>

You still seem very much alive for someone who has tasted death. Why not share your secret with the rest of us?

quests.name: Phantasmal Problems
quests.objective: Locate Vindael's unfinished sword and return it to him in Shen'dralas.
quests.description:
Ah, you look to be a sensible individual. Likely more sense than the last oaf that passed by. I need a small favor of you.

You see, I had a problem. My greatest masterpiece of swordsmithing was left unfinished before my passing, and I needed someone to assist in bringing it into the spirit world so that I may finish it. The last person was gracious enough to help, and they succeeded!

Now I have a new problem. Through every fault of his own, the previous adventurer can no longer bring it back to me.

quests.name: Spectral Iron Ore
quests.objective: Search for Spectral Iron Deposits around Shen'dralas and collect 10 Spectral Iron Ore. Return to Vindael in Shen'dralas once you have found enough.
quests.description:
Finally, FINALLY I can use this anvil for something other than a monumentally heavy table. I am delighted to finally hone my craft again after centuries of missed practice.

Now, you are probably thinking, "Vindael, this sounds like you are setting the stage for another request." And you would be correct!

I need to replenish my supply of iron, but your iron has a similar predicament to my blade. Fortunately, the solution is MUCH simpler.

<He hands you a ghostly pickaxe, without a chance to refuse.>
quests.progress: Regular iron just won't do, I'm afraid. By now I am sure you understand why.
quests.completion:
Wow, what a haul! You are tremendously helpful for someone that has to waste a third of your life sleeping. Where do you find the time to help a stranger out?

Ah, a reward? You were expecting a reward?

No, I don't think I'm quite ready to offer you one just yet.

quests.name: Tempered Expectations
quests.objective: Use the Phantasmal Blade to execute 8 wildlife in Shen'dralas, then return to Vindael at the temple.

objectives.text: Shen'dralas wildlife slain with the blade

quests.description:
Let me be the first to share that I was a master swordsman in life. I forged weapons by day and wielded them by night.

As you are quite well aware, my relationship with this particular blade is now extraordinarily complicated. Though I think I could swing it around, I'm not convinced it would be of much use unless I was fighting other spirits. Is that really of any value to me in Shen'dralas?

Nonetheless, I would like its capabilities tested and I think our forests could use a gentle culling.
quests.progress: How has that blade been working out for you?
quests.completion:
Marvelous! Spectacular even! After all these years, I am delighted to hear that this sword managed to shed blood at least once in its existence.

And those ghosts you saw--what an unexpected, peculiar surprise. I am less enthusiastic about that, as it likely means we will need to eradicate those same creatures a second time if they have managed to entangle themselves in our spirit realm.

Not a task I intend to bother you with, at least not today. Carry on with whatever it is you are doing here.

quests.name: Strange Pylons
quests.objective: Explore Shen'dralas in an effort to find other pylons like the one you found.
quests.description:
<You approach the strange crystal, guarded mere moments ago by emaciated mana elementals.

Its pedestal, though ancient, is noticeably less dilapidated than the elven ruins it is built upon.

A weak hum of power radiates from the fractured gemstone, but with its magic so heavily depleted its purpose will ultimately remain a mystery for the time being.

Perhaps there is more to discover nearby.>
quests.progress: A living <race>, all the way out here? Your presence honors me. I was beginning to think that I would spend the remainder of my mortality skulking in the shadows away from the centaur. To what do I owe this surprise encounter?
quests.completion:
To hear that the crystal within the temple shines brightly is an immense weight off my shoulders. I was worried that the centaur had breached the temple grounds now, too. It would seem they continue to be off-put by what's inside.

As for the other pylons, if elementals are still standing vigilant over them, then they are quite capable of being restored.

I hope the temple's denizens didn't frighten you. They are friendly enough, just bitter. Understandably bitter.

quests.name: A Brief History Lesson
quests.objective: Speak with Mordent Evenshade in Shen'dralas for information about the crystals you repaired.
quests.description:
You will have to forgive me for sending you on such a series of tasks without providing any context. I hadn't considered how suspicious this may have seemed, more so now that the skies have taken on such a dramatic appearance.

I will gladly answer your questions.
quests.progress: Do you have further questions?
quests.completion:
I hope that explanation alleviated any concerns you might have had, <name>. As you see, I was not acting out of any foul intent, and my failure to explain the situation thoroughly from the start was purely due to my enthusiasm of having a chance to see the crystals' lights shine again.

I am excited to visit the temple of Shen'dralas again, though it may take some time before I muster the courage to speak with the Shen'dralar there.

You, on the other hand...

quests.name: Bristleback Retreat
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and slay quilboar at Bristleback Retreat. Then report to Hagiak at the Magram Front on the other side of Valley of Bones in Desolace.
quests.description:
On the other side of the valley, we have established a small foothold to prepare to march into the forest nearby. Before you head straight there, I want you to deal with a recent Bristleback intrusion along the way. They seem to have arrived right around the same time we did, but managed to secure an artifact from the nearby temple that has kept us at bay.

This task is simple. Look for the thorns and the pigs. Kill a bunch, indiscriminately. Then report to Hagiak at the camp I mentioned.
quests.progress:
Ah. You must be the outsider running favors for Orgrul.

How lucky you are that you are terrible at sneaking around. Had my scouts not seen you stomping around on his behalf, your head would be on a bloodied pike.
quests.completion:
I am sorry you have come all this way, outsider, but you are not needed at the Magram front. Already you have distracted me long enough to delay our work.

Return to Orgrul and tell him--

On second thought, I do have something for a disposable soldier such as yourself. This will be quick, for better or worse.

quests.name: Long-Term Solutions
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram clan and slay 2 Outcast Scouts, 6 Outcast Marauders, and 8 Outcast Necromancers then return to Hagiak at the Magram Front.
quests.description:
There is a second centaur village out here, to the southwest. That one belongs to the Gelkis. You expect me to send you over just to spill some blood, right? Good. That had best be your first thought, else I would cast doubt on your allegiance to the Magram!

What are you waiting for? Go! Kill!
quests.completion:
My scouts have already reported your success. Now perhaps we can continue our training in peace. The Gelkis need to learn that this place, and the Desolace, belong to centaur born of Magram blood.

If you see any stragglers, cut off their heads too. They should be afraid to ever step hoof outside of their little hovel.

That will belong to us too, someday soon.

quests.name: Checking Things Out
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and investigate centaur points of interest within Shen'dralas. Then return to Nerlokh at the entrance of Valley of Bones with your findings.
quests.description:
We have all underestimated the power and presence of the Magram clan in this area, but this could prove an advantage.

With so many of their own distracted and their refusal to accept other clans' exiles, who is left to defend the village? What of their Khan?

I need you to go into the valley, deeper than you have gone before, and look around. If the Magram are as well fortified here as they seem, they may have left themselves vulnerable at their village...
quests.progress: Back already, <name>? What is the word?
quests.completion:
<You summarize your findings.>

Not one, but TWO camps?

<You clarify that one camp is unquestionably Magram, but the other looks to belong to the outcasts.>

This means that the Magram are likely in an active conflict. <name>, I think this may be our opportunity.

quests.name: Going Home
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and escort Rokren out of the Outcast Hideaway. Then inform Nerlokh near the Valley of Bones about what happened.

objectives.text: Escort Rokren out of the Outcast Hideaway

quests.description:
You! I saw you outside fighting the outcasts. I know not where you come from, but I need your help.

I was lured here by my Gelkis brethren with an assurance of safety. I knew the war in the Desolace was escalating beyond our control, but I never imagined my own people turning to necromancy in a convoluted bid to defect to the Magram clan. When I spoke out against this, they threatened to kill me if I ever stepped hoof outside this tent!

Please help.
quests.completion:
Rokren, yes! We spoke briefly as he passed by. I am grateful that he is alive and well.

Between the other Gelkis you rescued and Rokren, I am feeling a renewed sense of hope and courage. Our clan's true numbers are higher than we thought, and so many "outcasts" here were Gelkis lured out and held against their will.

There is a chance the Gelkis will survive this, <name>.

quests.name: Threat of Starvation
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and bring 6 Stolen Supplies back to Hagiak at the Magram Front.
quests.description:
Since you seem overly eager to help our clan, I am sure you would be willing to fetch some supplies while you are over in the Outcast Hideaway.

Felling our foes should be enough motivation for a Magram, but I see no reason why we could not profit from the endeavor, too.

When we have the exiles dealt with, we can secure this place for the Magram and raise an army to bring the other clans to their knees!
quests.progress: Slay their soldiers and starve the survivors. Their little hideaway should never be a sufficient staging ground against our clan again!
quests.completion:
<Hagiak peeks into several of the crates without a word at first.>

Of all things to bring out to the front lines, I would have never expected... nevermind. Some of these crates have food in them, and that's what matters. We've shortened the time they can survive here significantly.

The ultimate victory for our clan grows nearer.

quests.name: Return to Orgrul
quests.objective: Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and report back to Orgrul near the northern entrance to Valley of Bones.
quests.description:
You have done enough on the front lines. We can handle ourselves.

Tell Orgrul that you have served your purpose. The Magram Front is stronger now, and we have our sights set on the outcast encampment as our next settlement when another fleet of fighters joins the fray.

Well? Get going!
quests.completion:
An interesting development has unfolded within Magram Village during your brief absence. It was an act of war, carefully executed by an outsider fighting under the Gelkis banner.

Had this taken place a few months prior, I would have demanded execution of you and all other outsiders ignorantly playing deception with our clans.

But this is no ordinary circumstance.

This is an opportunity. For you, for the Magram, for the war.

quests.name: Forlorn Gardens
quests.objective: Investigate the Forlorn Gardens near Shen'dralas and then return to Mithera at the nearby temple.
quests.description:
As the garden's caretaker, it was my responsibility to ensure it thrived.

I knew there would come a day when I could no longer maintain it, so I enchanted a necklace gifted from my daughter to transform a new generation of saplings into treants, so they could watch over the garden in my stead. I placed it on an enchanted pedestal, sheltered within a small shrine.

The garden was in great hands. I must know what happened.
quests.progress:
When our pylons were at their weakest, I was unable to approach the garden to investigate the problem. Now that the haze has been lifted, I can't bring myself to get close again. I worry for the treants.

I do not want my memory of such a wonderful place to be further tainted.
quests.completion:
<Mithera listens quietly to your explanation of the situation.>

The pedestal is empty? My necklace is... missing?

<A great sadness washes over her expression.>

I should have expected as much. The quilboar and the centaur have been ravaging these lands for such a short amount of time, but the damage they have already done is immeasurable.

<name>, even if the magic is gone from the necklace, I am clinging onto hope that I may have it back. Would you be willing to help?

quests.name: What They've Done to My Peonies
quests.objective: Cull plants in the Forlorn Garden and then return to Mithera at Shen'dralas.
quests.description:
Please spare the details of how the life may have been twisted there. My heart is broken enough with the loss of my necklace.

But while I weep, the plants suffer.

<name>, I would like you to go back to the garden and cull some of the angered flora. Please be swift and merciful; they can feel pain, and they have been hurt enough. If you intend to go hunting for my necklace as well, I would ask you to prioritize that before visiting the gardens again... in the unlikely chance you find it.
quests.completion:
Eventually, I think the gardens will bloom beautifully again. Those flowers you culled today will give themselves back to the soil. It may take some time, perhaps a few generations, but someday it will be restored.

You have done a very kind deed, <name>. You have my personal gratitude.

quests.name: Meeting the Magister
quests.objective: Locate Magister Kirandis inside the temple of Shen'dralas.
quests.description:
I suspect your curiosity is luring you toward the grand structure now, yes? Good!

The Shen'dralar there are unlikely to welcome you with open arms, but so long as you tread respectfully, I do not think you will run into any trouble.

With any luck, my old friend Kirandis might be easy to find. Of everyone, he is the most likely to be amicable to your presence.
quests.completion:
It is remarkable to see that the pylons' power burns brightly once more. I am surprised I hadn't noticed before you arrived. I was beginning to think that this one would soon suffer the same fate, and we would be lost to time.

Thank you for tethering us back in full to Shen'dralas. Try to meet some of our denizens. They may be wary of you, but that will pass.

quests.name: Word of the Woods
quests.objective: Find Woodwyrd in the Forlorn Gardens at Shen'dralas in the Desolace.
quests.description:
Among the treants borne of the necklace, one in particular stood above all the others to have received the gift of life and sentience. I suspect if they have fallen, he may be the only one that remains.

He spent his days tending to each and every bloom and bud, and his evenings rooted in the ground to serve as a nest for the smaller critters.

If he is alive, and I pray that to be true, then he may know what happened.

I am holding out hope for my good friend, Woodwyrd.
quests.completion:
It is too late. For these gardens.

I am the last of my generation of caretakers. Without the gift, more cannot take my place.

The weeds have overtaken the land. The flowers are restless. The trees wither.

<Woodwyrd slowly turns toward the towering ancient illuminating the sky with its endless fire.>

quests.name: Powering the Pylons
quests.objective: Acquire the Mana Sieve from within the temple in Shen'dralas and use it to collect Ancient Mana Crystals. Once you have acquired enough mana, empower the pylons and return to Mordent Evenshade.
quests.description:
You may have seen the floating sparks of mana scattered throughout Shen'dralas. This is a new phenomenon, likely the result of the damage the pylons have endured.

We need this mana back in a semicrystallized form. We can accomplish this by using the Mana Sieve found within the temple. Borrow the sieve and collect any floating mana orbs you find.

The temple's denizens will not appreciate their precious artifact being borrowed without their consent, but they will understand in time.
quests.progress: It is good to see you again, <name>.
quests.completion:
I see you have successfully repaired the pylons--how could I not notice?

<Mordent gestures up and toward the skies, his gaze briefly followed in that direction as well. As his attention returns to you, he lofts his brow as he takes note of your seemingly lesser levels of enthusiasm.>

quests.name: A Heart of Crystal
quests.objective: Slay a Decrepit Pylon Protector for their Depleted Crystal Heart and bring it to Historian Biraxas within the temple of Shen'dralas.
quests.description:
While I watched in horror as you frolicked through the haunted woods with my precious relic, your meddling did inspire an idea.

The unstable rifts you encountered are the precursors to our pylon guards. We have been unable to conjure more for centuries, and I worry what might happen when those that remain inevitably flicker out.

I know it seems counterintuitive, but see if you can find another pylon protector nearly on the verge of collapse and recover their Crystal Heart. I'll explain more after.
quests.progress: I assure you I am not looking to sabotage one of our only means of defense. If a protector does not look as lively and well-nourished as those in our temple, then they are on the last hundred years or so of their lifecycle. If anything, it is a mercy killing.
quests.completion:
You were successful, I see! And what a heart you recovered. I am excited to know that the passing of centuries did little to tarnish the craftsmanship of this gemstone.

Most importantly, this is a promising discovery. It would seem that, indeed, mana is temporary, but gemstones are forever.

Are you eager to learn what comes next?

quests.name: Mana Mania
quests.objective: Throw the Depleted Crystal Heart into an Unstable Mana Rift. Return to Historian Biraxas within the temple of Shen'dralas with proof of success or failure.
quests.description:
While sourcing the gems necessary to conjure the elementals is a challenge itself, the bigger concern is whether there is still enough loose mana in Shen'dralas to create them. With this heart, we can confirm once and for all whether we need to begin researching other means of defense.

For you, the task is simple. Simply toss this gem into one of those unstable rifts. If we're lucky, you'll have a fight on your hands. Don't feel compelled to hold back, if it works once, it will work again.
quests.completion:
It worked! It worked!!

I struggle to find words, <name>! I did not expect this to prove successful. With each passing decade I worried that whatever chance there might have been had passed.

This may seem unimportant or perhaps even mundane to you, but rest assured that this is unlife changing for us.

I will begin planning next steps. I have no further tasks for you, but others might appreciate your aid.

Thank you. Truly.

quests.name: Partially Digested Collar
quests.objective: Return the Partially Digested Collar to someone who knows about it. Presumably, they can be found in or near Shen'dralas in Desolace.
quests.description:
<You hold a grimy collar retrieved from the belly of a slain creature. The material is of a high-quality leather, clearly stitched with care.

A tag dangles from a corroded buckle. You swipe away the gunk and can see Thalassian text, though the letters are stylized beyond readability, perhaps even to those familiar with the language.

Now, you are presented with a choice. Do you disregard this and move on with your life, or do you attempt the impossible and seek to bring closure to its owner?>
quests.progress: <Liranne takes the collar and inspects it. She gently cradles the metal tag in her other hand, and flashes a brief smile upon reading it.>
quests.completion:
This belonged to Dahlia, my best friend and favorite feline. Dahlia... I never was creative with names. It fit her though, she was a vibrant, blooming flower in my life.

The origin of it isn't very exciting. I was passing by some dahlia flowers in the garden when this little kitten leapt out at me! So playfully menacing. She followed me back to the temple and... that was that!

No need to stick around while I reminisce. Here's something for your trouble, thank you for resurfacing some old memories.

quests.name: Corpsefeeder's Carapace
quests.objective: Find someone interested in Corpsefeeder's Carapace.
quests.description:
<With a terrible crunch, you removed a piece of the worm's carapace upon its demise.

Despite its enormous size and hefty weight, it is disappointingly ordinary. This creature was seemingly not the result of a cruel experiment nor carefully bred to be an all-devouring beast.

It is simply an impressive shell, likely desired only by collectors. Perhaps you could find one, though other than the centaur, who else might be alive around here?>
quests.progress: <Kog'thug has a blade to your throat before you manage to say a word.>
quests.completion:
<The quilboar's eyes dart over toward the carapace jutting out from your backpack. He snorts once. Twice. Three times even, before pulling his blade away.>

Big Worm dead?

Big Worm dig through Bristleback land. Eat our dead. Devour our young.

Big worm dead. Big <race> hero of Bristleback. Big <race> allowed in quilboar land. For now.

What Big <race> want?

quests.name: Passing the Blame
quests.objective: Seek out a quilboar of significance at the Bristleback Retreat.
quests.description:
If you wish to recover the woman's gift, march north into the Valley of Bones.

It was stolen. The quilboar are to blame. I saw it. With my own two eyebulbs.

They are why this garden is doomed to die.

Do not forgive them.
quests.completion:
Big <race> want necklace? Well, Big <race> can't have!

Thornweavers need necklace. Land is deader than dead. Thorns no sprout without necklace! Centaur tread where thorns no sprout. See problem, or Big <race> blind?

Kog'thug have idea. Want trade?

quests.name: Not on Squealing Terms
quests.objective: Quell the quilboar's quarrel by bringing Quolga a Benevolent Bouquet and the Virulent Blood of Agamaggan. The flowers to make the bouquet can be acquired at the Forlorn Gardens, near Shen'dralas in the Desolace.
quests.description:
Quolga the Wise is Kog'thug's life mate. Quolga great thornweaver, that why Kog'thug like her. Quolga also has necklace Big <race> seeks.

Problem? We not on squealing terms. She mad we stole necklace in first place. Then why use it? That what Kog'thug want know!

BUT! Quolga like flowers as much as thorns. Know where we can get flowers? Where we got necklace!

Maybe she not be mad at Kog'thug if Big <race> bring flowers and this blood for him? Maybe she trade necklace!

Tell her Kog'thug sorry.
quests.progress:
<Quolga looks at you with a confused expression and nearly-crossed eyes.>

What you want with Quolga? Did Kog'thug send you, too?
quests.completion:
I see. Kog'thug never say sorry face-to-face. Always sending someone to speak for him. Are these flowers from him? Or did Kog'thug send you to fetch these too?

<Quolga listens to your overly truthful explanation of the situation. The thornweaver is extremely unamused by the facts and heaves out a sigh.>

Stupid boar.

This trinket ran out of power weeks ago and no longer serves us any purpose.

It's yours now. Leave the blood. Keep the flowers.

Go away.

quests.name: Forlorn Necklace
quests.objective: Bring the Forlorn Necklace to Mithera at the temple of Shen'dralas in the Desolace.
quests.description:
<The necklace you have been seeking is at last in your possession, but unfortunately the magic contained within has been entirely depleted. While not ideal for your current situation, at least it made its acquisition from the quilboar relatively easy.

It is probably best to bring this back to Mithera.>
quests.progress:
<Mithera stares toward the gardens. She did not notice you approach, at least until you entered into her field of view.>

Hello again, <name>. I am grateful to see you again, though I expect you do not bring good news.
quests.completion:
Is that my daughter's necklace? Oh <name>... I assumed the worst.

You are saying the quilboar had this? I am truly surprised that they took such good care of it. But...

I can no longer feel the magic within. This is terrible news, <name>, but it is something we can address. For now, I need to consider our options... and gather my feelings.

Return to me again in the future. For now, I need time to ponder.

quests.name: Tattered Journal
quests.objective: The text suggests the author of this journal may be somewhere in Shen'dralas.
quests.description:
<Found near Shen'dralas, this dirty old tome no longer holds most of its knowledge.

Of the text that remains, individual letters are difficult to distinguish from words. It may prove challenging to read at first, but one of them appears to be a surname.

Perhaps its author, "Evenshade", may be found nearby.>
quests.progress: Is there something you need?
quests.completion:
My journal? Certainly not, it was lost centuries ago.

<Mordent reclaims the dirty tome and examines the cover. His brow lifts in surprise, but it falls after he opens the covers.>

You have indeed found my journal, but alas, all that I had written is gone. I have not forgotten what was within, but I do not wish to speak any of it aloud.

Should its pages have also survived somehow, you have my permission to attempt to restore it.
